meta.title: PostgreSQL Types Reference - S-Jiffy
meta.description: 60+ PostgreSQL data types with storage size, value range, and description; click a type name to copy it.
desc: 60+ PostgreSQL data types with storage size, value range, and description; click a type name to copy it.
ui.2: Click a type name to copy it, ready to paste directly into SQL.
ui.5: OID alias type referencing a table.
ui.8: WAL log location, used for replication and recovery.
ui.14: Full-text search: preprocessed lexeme list, paired with GIN indexes.
ui.16: UUID universally unique identifier, suitable for distributed primary keys.
ui.18: All types can be declared as arrays, e.g. int[3][3].
ui.24: Network address (mask bits must be valid).
ui.27: Polygon represented by a closed path.
ui.28: Path made of a point sequence (open or closed).
ui.30: Line segment defined by two endpoints.
ui.31: Infinite line defined by two points.
ui.33: JSON binary format with indexing (GIN) and efficient queries; recommended by default.
ui.34: JSON text, preserves whitespace, key order, and duplicate keys.
ui.35: Time + time zone offset, generally not recommended.
ui.38: Date + time with time zone (stored internally as UTC).
ui.39: Date + time without time zone, p is fractional seconds precision (0-6).
ui.41: Internal name type used for system catalogs.
ui.42: Variable-length string without length limit; PostgreSQL's recommendation for long text.
ui.43: Monetary type with localized currency symbol, 2 decimal places precision.
ui.44: Auto-incrementing big integer, equivalent to bigint + sequence.
ui.45: Auto-incrementing integer, equivalent to integer + sequence.
ui.46: Auto-incrementing small integer, equivalent to smallint + sequence.
ui.49: Arbitrary-precision number, alias numeric; suitable for amounts and exact calculations.
ui.51: Common integer type, aliases int, int4.
